# Draft:Kazakh–Dzungar War (1708–1712)

}}
The Kazakh–Dzungar war of 1708–1712 was a military struggle between the Kazakh Khanate and the Dzungar Khanate.
Background
In 1698, Tsewang Rabtan had attacked the Kazakhs as the Kazakhs had raided and caused trouble in Dzungaria, defeating their forces and pursuing them to Chu and Talas river valleys, killing thousands and capturing about 10,000 men.
Course of conflict
In 1708, a small detachment of troops invaded the Kazakh Khanate, against the Senior Jüz devastating the nearby areas and forcing the population to flee to Tashkent. They soon launched another offensive in 1709, causing a meeting on Karakum desert, by the representatives of all jüzes and agreeing to let Bogembai batyr to lead the Kazakh army in which he move in order to repel them back to Dzungaria. In 1710, the Senior and Middle Jüz started resisting against the Dzungars. During 1711–1712, Bogenbai had successfully repelled the Dzungar detachment.
